sentences.text: Plotopterum is an extinct genus of flightless seabirds from the North Pacific, containing only one described species, Plotopterum joaquinensis.
The genus name combines a prefix meaning 'swimming' with a suffix meaning 'wing'.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was roughly the size of a Brandt's cormorant but narrower and more rounded.
Unlike the flightless cormorant, the wings of Plotopterum were heavily specialized for swimming rather than reduced, and the swollen shape of the triosseal area strengthened the wing for swimming.
An individual attributed to Plotopterum was approximately the size of a great cormorant.
The swollen shape of the triosseal area strengthened the wing for swimming.
The holotype of Plotopterum was discovered in 1961 in the San Joaquin Valley of California by Dick Bishop and Ed Mitchell.
In 1985, Hasegawa and Storrs L. Olson redescribed Japanese fossil remains as belonging to the genus Plotopterum.
Plotopterum belongs to the family Plotopteridae.
Plotopterum lived in the North Pacific during the Late Oligocene and Early Miocene, between 23.04 and 15.98 million years ago.
Plotopterum was likely limited to coastal waters.
The flightlessness of Plotopterum is inferred rather than confirmed due to a lack of well-preserved remains.
